bibliographic-data.invention-title: CLOSED-LOOP CAVITATION-PLASMA THERMOELECTRIC FLUID PURIFICATION CORE AND DISTRIBUTED INDUSTRIAL, CIVIC, TRANSIT, ROBOTIC, ARMOR, AND OFF-WORLD ARCHITECTURES

description.p: TECHNICAL FIELD: The present invention relates to closed-loop thermal-electric power generation, hydrodynamic cavitation, nanosecond pulsed plasma mineralization, zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) water purification, and integrated architectures spanning industrial, municipal, subterranean civic, transoceanic transit, biomimetic robotics, kinetic/DEW-harvesting armor, atmospheric-condensing propulsion/weapons, and planetary/orbital systems.

SUMMARY OF CORE ARCHITECTURE (FIGS. 1–3): A modular Cool Power Core™ (100) preheats contaminated or ambient water to 90°C using recovered enthalpy (102), induces intense acoustic-hydrodynamic cavitation across CVD-graphene nozzles (104), mineralizes PFAS, pathogens, and toxic gases via 33.6 kV ZVS nanosecond plasma discharges (106), and harvests net 48 VDC surplus power (+335.6 We/core mean) via dual-stage thermoelectric/ORC converters (108) while condensing >=98.5% pure distillate (112).

RADIOLYTIC, WEARABLE, ROBOTIC & SWARM EXTENSIONS (FIGS. 4–11): Continuation embodiments incorporate 4H-SiC / HfO2-graphene betavoltaic and gamma-voltaic liners (402), 37°C human metabolic-heat exoskeleton life support (600), tri-necked continuum biomimetic robotic mounts (800), and hermaphroditic 48V / 90°C peer-to-peer swarm docking umbilicals (1004).

FRONTIER PLASMA TOOLS, TERRAFORMING & SUB-GLACIAL ROVERS (FIGS. 12–17): Further embodiments provide a 0.65 T Halbach-Bitter magnetically confined handheld Martian plasma lance (1200) with <1.2 ms GaN deadman quench (1304), a 6,000 m abyssal hydrothermal plasma torch (1400), a zero-recoil (<0.15 N) asteroid volatile rock-splitter (1500), an atmospheric terraforming spire (1600), and a 10^8 Gy acoustic-cavitation ice-melt rover (1700).

TRANSOCEANIC TRANSIT, FLOATING/ORBITAL HUBS & SUBTERRANEAN CITIES (FIGS. 18–23): Large-scale civic embodiments include submerged tension-leg transoceanic maglev tubes (1802) with <= +0.08 K thermal impact, zero-brine oceanic mineral extraction hubs (2000), counter-rotating orbital colonies (2100), and radiation-shielded linear ridge-and-valley subterranean cities (2200) on degraded terrain.

KINETIC/DEW-HARVESTING ARMOR & ATMOSPHERIC-CONDENSING TRI-MODE WEAPON (FIGS. 24–25): Wearable defense embodiments integrate a dielectric Bragg mirror + B4C shell (2404), 4H-SiC TPV-TEG converter (2406), and 18 mm NASA viscoelastic memory-foam + piezo-PVDF layer (2408) (e <= 0.04) feeding a supercapacitor (2414) that drives an 18,000 RPM cyclone (2502), -78°C cryo-mold (2504), 33.6 kV plasma-sintering exciter (2506), and linear coilgun/plasma/laser tri-mode weapon (2500).

claim.claim-text: 1. A closed-loop thermal-electric and fluid-purification core (100), comprising: a preheated fluid reservoir (102) maintained at approximately 90°C by waste-heat recovery; a CVD-graphene acoustic-hydrodynamic cavitation chamber (104) coupled to said reservoir (102); a 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (106) mineralizing contaminants into inert solids; a dual-stage thermoelectric and organic Rankine power module (108) bridging said 90°C reservoir (102) against a cold sink (110) to output 48 VDC net surplus power; and a condenser (112) recovering at least 98.5% pure distillate.

2. The core (100) of claim 1, wherein the cavitation chamber (104) comprises multi-layer chemical-vapor-deposited graphene nozzles generating localized micro-bubble collapse temperatures exceeding 4,500 K.

3. The core (100) of claim 1, wherein the ZVS pulsed plasma reactor (106) delivers 12 ns pulses at 33.6 kV peak potential to achieve >6-Log destruction of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and pathogens.
4. The core (100) of claim 1, further comprising a solid-state graphene-CNT supercapacitor bank (114) regulating a 48 VDC bus.

5. A method of simultaneous power generation and zero-liquid-discharge water purification, comprising: heating contaminated influent to 90°C using industrial or environmental enthalpy (102); inducing hydrodynamic cavitation across a CVD-graphene throat (104); subjecting vapor-liquid phases to 33.6 kV nanosecond plasma discharges (106); and extracting net electrical work across a thermal gradient (108) while condensing pure water (112).
6. The method of claim 5, wherein net continuous electrical export exceeds 320 We per 382.93 Wth of recovered thermal offset.
7. A modular containerized tri-generation skid comprising an array of 100 to 1,000 cores (100) of claim 1 coupled in parallel to a common 48 VDC/480 VAC inverter manifold (116).

8. A radiolytic-thermal energy harvesting core (400), comprising: the closed-loop core (100) of claim 1; a radiation-shielded pressure vessel lined with 4H-SiC and HfO2-graphene betavoltaic/gamma-voltaic conversion layers (402); and a radiolysis-assisted plasma chamber (404) utilizing ionizing flux from spent nuclear fuel, tritium, or cosmic radiation to reduce ZVS plasma excitation draw.
9. The core (400) of claim 8, wherein the betavoltaic/gamma-voltaic liners (402) contribute +16.5 to +21.5 We of continuous direct electrical conversion per core.
10. The core (400) of claim 8, further comprising a Pd-23%Ag permeation membrane (406) separating tritium and deuterium isotopes at >99.99% purity.
11. The core (400) of claim 8, utilizing Sm2Co17 high-temperature magnets and silicon-on-insulator (SOI) electronics rated to >10^8 Gy total ionizing dose.

12. A nuclear reactor or spent-fuel dry-cask bottoming system comprising a plurality of cores (400) of claim 8 thermally coupled to secondary condenser loops without penetrating primary reactor containment.
13. The system of claim 12, wherein amidoxime-eluted seawater uranium yellowcake (U3O8) is concurrently precipitated and harvested.

14. A wearable metabolic-heat life-support exoskeleton core (600), comprising: a micro-scale closed-loop core (100) having a mass under 3.5 kg; a conformal liquid-cooling undergarment (602) capturing 37°C human metabolic heat; a micro-plasma urine and sweat mineralizer (604) recovering 98.5% potable water and electrolytic O2; and a thermoelectric generator (606) bridging the 37°C/90°C loop against ambient air or space.
15. The exoskeleton core (600) of claim 14, generating +24.5 to +28.0 We of continuous autonomous power for joint actuators and environmental sensors.
16. The exoskeleton core (600) of claim 14, further comprising a solid-amine CO2 scrubber (608) regenerated at 90°C by the core reservoir.
17. The exoskeleton core (600) of claim 14, integrated into a sealed EVA spacesuit or hazardous-environment HazMat suit providing >480 hours of closed-loop autonomy.

18. A method of powering a wearable powered exoskeleton using wearer metabolic heat (602), comprising circulating a working fluid across the wearer's torso at 37°C, boosting enthalpy via actuator regenerative braking, and driving a micro-cavitation plasma life-support cycle (604).
19. The method of claim 18, wherein carbon dioxide is electrochemically reduced into solid carbon and breathable oxygen.

20. An autonomous biomimetic robotic platform (800), comprising: an articulated quadruped or humanoid chassis (802) driven by quasi-direct-drive (QDD) brushless actuators; an onboard thermal-electric core (804) harvesting QDD stator and regenerative braking heat into a 90°C loop; and an atmospheric or ambient-water intake (806) replenishing closed-loop working fluid via 33.6 kV plasma purification.
21. The robotic platform (800) of claim 20, comprising three telescoping omni-flexible continuum necks (808) terminating in convertible sensor-manipulator hands.
22. The robotic platform (800) of claim 20, further comprising a 38.5°C heated tandem saddle (810) supporting two human riders and cargo.
23. The robotic platform (800) of claim 20, incorporating deployable NIJ-IV ballistic shield wings (812) and an 8-DOF prehensile tail manipulator (814).
24. A wildfire-fighting or hazardous-rescue autonomous quadruped (800) of claim 20 utilizing ambient fire-front thermal gradients (>200°C) to boost continuous electrical generation above 650 We.
25. The quadruped of claim 24, projecting a high-velocity water-mist and plasma-radical fire-suppression plume from its continuum nozzles (808).

26. A peer-to-peer autonomous swarm energy and fluid sharing network (1000), comprising: a plurality of mobile robotic units (1002), each housing an onboard core (100); and hermaphroditic magnetic-latching coaxial umbilicals (1004) transferring both 48 VDC electrical power and 90°C pressurized thermal water between units.
27. The network (1000) of claim 26, wherein a stationary anchor unit harvests high-ΔT environmental heat and distributes 90°C working fluid to mobile scout units.
28. The network (1000) of claim 26, further comprising a ballistic phalanx formation controller (1006) interlocking deployable shield wings across adjacent units.
29. The network (1000) of claim 26, wherein coaxial couplings (1004) purge and sterilize fluid interfaces with 33.6 kV plasma prior to decoupling.
30. The network (1000) of claim 26, supporting transmedium underwater-to-air autonomous drones docking at sea-surface buoys.
31. The network (1000) of claim 26, operating over decentralized mesh optical/RF telemetry without central cloud infrastructure.

32. A handheld magnetically confined planetary plasma lance (1200), comprising: a hilt housing a micro-core (1202) with a 180 mL water/ice cartridge (1204), 90°C CVD-graphene cavitator (1206), and 33.6 kV ZVS plasma exciter (1208); a hybrid 0.42 T Sm2Co17 Halbach array (1210) and +0.23 T CuCrZr Bitter coil (1212) forming a 0.65 T throat and 0.67 T distal magnetic mirror pinch confining a 0.92 m, 4,200 K plasma blade (1214); and external cryo-fins (1216) bridging against -60°C Martian atmosphere to regenerate +142.0 We.
33. The handheld plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, further comprising a coaxial vacuum aspiration shroud (1218) recovering >98% of ionized working vapor for closed-loop recycling.

34. The handheld plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, comprising a capacitive EVA-glove deadman sensor (1302) triggering solid-state GaN quench switches (1304) to collapse the magnetic bottle in <1.2 ms upon grip release.
35. The handheld plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, wherein plasma beta is maintained at β ≤ 0.18 in a 610 Pa CO2 atmosphere.
36. The handheld plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, powered by a 140 Wh graphene-CNT supercapacitor (1306) delivering 3.5 kW peak cutting pulses.
37. The handheld plasma lance (1200) of claim 32, selectively switchable between permafrost core boring, Ti-6Al-4V welding, and basalt rock cutting modes.

38. A deep-sea hydrothermal plasma torch (1400) rated to 6,000 m depth (60.8 MPa), comprising: a titanium-niobium pressure hull housing a closed-loop core (1402); an arc-shroud heat recuperator (1404) feeding a 90°C cavitation-plasma generator; a 0.75 T magnetic nozzle emitting a 4.2 kW, 6,800 K hydro-sheathed plasma jet (1406); and hull-conformal thermoelectric exchangers (1408) bridging against 2.0°C abyssal seawater to regenerate +196.4 We.
39. The deep-sea plasma torch (1400) of claim 38, operating without umbilical surface power cables for subsea salvage and polymetallic sulfide nodule cutting.
40. The deep-sea plasma torch (1400) of claim 38, wherein an annular high-velocity steam-gas sheath isolates the 6,800 K plasma core from hydrostatic quenching.

41. A zero-recoil asteroid microgravity plasma rock-splitter (1500), comprising: a 3.2 kW, 5,400 K magnetically pinched plasma needle (1502) flash-vaporizing bound phyllosilicate water inside asteroid regolith to induce 45–90 MPa internal spallation with <0.15 N axial recoil; a coaxial volatile capture hood (1504) aspirating released H2O, CO2, and metal carbonyl vapors into a 90°C closed-loop core (1506); and a 120 K shaded radiator (1508) generating +184.0 We.
42. The rock-splitter (1500) of claim 41, achieving >100% net fluid replenishment from mined hydrated asteroid minerals.
43. The rock-splitter (1500) of claim 41, separating nickel and iron carbonyls (Ni(CO)4, Fe(CO)5) for zero-gravity additive manufacturing.

44. A closed-loop atmospheric terraforming and climate-restoration spire (1600), comprising: an array of 1,000 cores (1602) integrated within a vertical intake pylon; a 33.6 kV ZVS plasma-catalytic reactor (1604) splitting atmospheric CO2 and regolith perchlorates into breathable O2, solid carbon/CNT feedstock, and ammonium nitrate fertilizer; and a ground-coupled geothermal or cryogenic radiator sink (1606) exporting >329 kWe continuous net power.
45. The spire (1600) of claim 44, configured for Martian 610 Pa / -60°C surface operation to produce >1,027 kg/day O2 and >386 kg/day solid carbon nanotubes.
46. The spire (1600) of claim 44, configured for Earth climate restoration to mineralize >6,450 kg/day CO2 and distill >12,960 L/day pure water.

47. A sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal rover (1700), comprising: a 10^8 Gy radiation-hardened hull (1702) housing four cores (1704) with 4H-SiC betavoltaic liners; a forward 33.6 kV plasma acoustic-cavitation ice-fracturing nosecone (1706) boring through >15 km of 95 K cryogenic ice; and articulating seafloor tracks (1708) harvesting 140°C hydrothermal vent plumes against 2°C abyssal ocean water.
48. The rover (1700) of claim 47, generating +1,488 We during ice descent and +1,424 We during >10-year autonomous seafloor exploration.
49. The rover (1700) of claim 47, utilizing acoustic-cavitation shockwaves to fracture cryogenic ice ahead of thermal melt contact.

50. A closed-loop thermal-harvesting evacuated maglev transit system (1800), comprising: a low-pressure guideway tube (1802); vacuum roughing-pump stations thermally coupled to arrays of cores (1804) bridging 95°C pump compression and linear-stator heat against subsurface geothermal piles or deep-ocean water (1806); and passenger pods carrying onboard micro-cores (1808) providing zero-discharge cabin air and water recycling.

51. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, wherein the guideway tube (1802) is a positively buoyant submerged transoceanic conduit suspended 150 to 300 m below sea level via tension-leg tethers (1810) spaced at 250 m intervals.
52. The transit system (1800) of claim 51, limiting benthic seafloor contact to <0.012 km2 per 1,000 km and thermal plume rise to <= +0.08 K at 1.0 m.
53. The transit system (1800) of claim 51, incorporating 6-DOF seismic gimbals (1902) surviving Mw 9.2 fault displacements up to 6.5 m.
54. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, wherein subsea methane-seep plasma mineralizers (1904) oxidize continental-shelf CH4 plumes.
55. The transit system (1800) of claim 50, offsetting >82% of steady-state tube vacuum maintenance power while exporting surplus grid electricity.

56. A floating oceanic sanctuary and zero-brine marine mineral hub (2000), comprising: semi-submersible spar pontoons (2002) supporting a Category-5 rated climate-controlled ETFE geodesic canopy (2004); an array of >10,000 cores (2006) bridging process heat against 2°C–4°C abyssal seawater; and a zero-liquid-discharge crystallizer (2008) extracting pure water, battery-grade Li2CO3, Mg(OH)2, and amidoxime U3O8 with zero hypersaline brine outfall.
57. The oceanic hub (2000) of claim 56, integrated above a -200 m submerged transoceanic maglev transfer terminal (2010).
58. The oceanic hub (2000) of claim 56, skimming and plasma-mineralizing floating ocean microplastics into pure water and inert carbon.

59. An orbital artificial-gravity colony and cislunar mass-driver hub (2100), comprising: two counter-rotating torus rings (2102) generating 1.00 g around a non-rotating central electromagnetic mass-driver dock (2104); a 2.4 m water-wall radiation shield (2106); and 25,000 cores (2108) bridging solar-foundry and cosmic-ray radiolytic heat against an 85 K shaded deep-space radiator (2110).
60. The orbital colony (2100) of claim 59, recovering 99.85% of water and synthesizing >1,685 kg/day of structural carbon nanotubes from closed-loop CO2.
61. The orbital colony (2100) of claim 59, harvesting mass-driver linear-motor braking enthalpy during cislunar cargo capture.

62. A radiation-shielded linear ridge-and-valley subterranean megastructure (2200) sited on degraded terrain, comprising: an elongated aerodynamic hill shell (2202) having 22°–26° exterior slopes covered by a 2.2 m to 4.0 m living soil and vegetation radiation mantle (2204) attenuating >96% of cosmic/solar radiation; an open V-shaped central canyon with staggered sunlit residential garden terraces (2206); a multi-level subterranean commerce and autonomous logistics spine (2208); and a distributed array of closed-loop thermal-electric cores (2210).
63. The megastructure (2200) of claim 62, wherein wind-saddle passes (2212) sculpted across the ridge crest channel natural weather patterns and passive valley ventilation.
64. The megastructure (2200) of claim 62, sited on open-pit mine scars and utilizing 33.6 kV plasma reactors to remediate Acid Mine Drainage into pure water and inert vitrified slag.

65. A method of constructing a high-density self-sufficient metropolis without displacing arable land, comprising: excavating a subterranean commerce canyon (2208) within degraded desert, strip-mine, or permafrost terrain; erecting stepped sunlit residential terraces (2206); blanketing exterior flanks with >2.2 m of living soil (2204); and operating distributed cores (2210) to achieve >85% food, >92% material, and >100% power/water self-sufficiency.
66. The method of claim 65, incorporating an automated underground shuttle spine (2302) delivering goods directly into residential pantries within 12 minutes.
67. The method of claim 65, deployed within a subterranean Martian lava tube beneath >50 m of basalt overburden (2304) using heliostat solar mirrors.

68. A kinetic and directed-energy-weapon (DEW) harvesting exoskeleton armor system (2400), comprising: a multi-layer modular armor plate (2402) having an outer dielectric Bragg mirror and boron carbide (B4C) shell (2404) reflecting >92% of laser energy; a 4H-SiC thermophotovoltaic (TPV) and Bi2Te3 thermoelectric layer (2406) converting absorbed thermal flux into electrical pulses; an 18 mm open-cell viscoelastic memory-foam and piezo-PVDF kinetic layer (2408) exhibiting a coefficient of restitution e <= 0.04 and converting >96% of ballistic impact energy into electricity and heat; and a 37°C micro-channel cooling liner (2410) coupled to a dorsal closed-loop core (2412).

69. The armor system (2400) of claim 68, attenuating >180 g ballistic shock down to <14.5 g while harvesting >1,180 J per rifle impact and +640 to +1,850 We during DEW exposure into a graphene-CNT supercapacitor (2414).
70. The armor system (2400) of claim 68, utilizing tool-free quick-disconnect latches (2416) for interchangeable field replacement of armor modules.

71. An atmospheric-condensing tri-mode return-fire weapon (2500) powered by the supercapacitor (2414) of claim 69, comprising: an 18,000 RPM cyclonic intake (2502) aspirating ambient atmospheric gases and airborne particulates; a -78°C cryogenic condensation mold (2504) coupled to the cold side of a closed-loop core; a 33.6 kV ZVS plasma-sintering exciter (2506) solidifying condensed gases and particulates into a dense solid projectile; and a multi-stage linear induction coilgun barrel (2508) accelerating said projectile to >1,400 m/s.

72. The weapon (2500) of claim 71, selectively switchable between solid atmospheric-condensed slugs (2510), 4,800 K magnetically pinched plasma bolts (2512), and 1,064 nm pulsed Yb:YAG laser bursts (2514).
73. The weapon (2500) of claim 71, operating on Earth, Mars (CO2/regolith dust), or Titan (CH4/tholin aerosol) without external metallic ammunition magazines.

abstract.p: A closed-loop thermal-electric and fluid-purification system (100) preheats influent water to 90°C using recovered waste or environmental enthalpy (102), induces hydrodynamic cavitation across CVD-graphene nozzles (104), and applies 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond pulsed plasma (106) to achieve >6-Log mineralization of PFAS, pathogens, and toxic gases into inert solids while condensing >=98.5% pure distillate (112). Dual-stage thermoelectric and Rankine converters (108) bridge the 90°C loop against cold sinks (110) to generate continuous 48 VDC net electrical power (+335.6 We/core mean). Integrated embodiments span radiolytic harvesting (400), wearable metabolic exoskeletons (600), tri-necked robotic mounts (800), swarm docking (1000), planetary plasma lances (1200) and rock-splitters (1500), terraforming spires (1600), sub-glacial rovers (1700), submerged transoceanic maglev tubes (1800), floating/orbital hubs (2000, 2100), radiation-shielded linear subterranean cities (2200), kinetic/DEW-harvesting viscoelastic-TPV armor (2400), and atmospheric-condensing tri-mode coilgun/plasma/laser weapons (2500).
